newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 3.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on June 3. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Indonesia's President Suharto has asked scholars under the Indonesian Moslem Intellectual Association (ICMI) to study the cause of riots that rocked the country during the election campaign and the May 29 polling day.

The Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) has said last week's general election served as bad political education to the people because it had been riddled with vote rigging and cheating. The party said it had found that 99.9 percent of poll rigging cases were committed by government officials who meant to help the ruling Golkar party.

The conflict-ridden Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) may be forced to relinquish the House of Representatives seats it won in the May 29 general elections if it does not make the minimum representation of 11 seats. The PDI suffered a massive defeat in the election, securing only ten House seats for its 744 legislative candidates.

Bank Mashill, Bank ANZ Panin and Bank Hanil Tamara have been voted the country's best banks by the Info Bank magazine. Info Bank evaluated the banks on, among others, their capital asset ratio, net interest margin, return on average assets and efficiency.

The East Java election committee has decided that a re-vote in Sampang on Madura island will be held on June 4. Thousands of people rioted last Thursday night, burning houses, offices and a church, alleging vote riggging after the ruling Golkar party appeared to be sweeping the elections on the island off eastern Java.
